ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are 7 empty circles, arranged overall in a triangle. It can be seen that there are five straight lines, each passing through 3 circles: the left oblique line, the central vertical line, the right oblique line, the middle horizontal line, and the bottom horizontal line. Denote the topmost circle as T. The problem requires filling the circles with 1 to 7 each used once, and the sum of the three numbers on each straight line is the same; let this common sum be S. Then reason: Adding the sums of the five lines gives 5S. According to the connection relationship in the figure, the top circle T is on the three lines of the left oblique line, the central vertical line, and the right oblique line, so it is counted 3 times; the other 6 circles are each on two lines, so each is counted 2 times. The total sum of 1 to 7 is 28, therefore the total of the five line sums is 2×28+T=56+T. Thus 56+T must be divisible by 5. T can only be one number from 1 to 7; checking gives that 56+4=60 can be divisible by 5, and the other numbers do not satisfy this. Therefore the top circle should be filled with 4.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: it has 7 circles arranged as a triangle, with five straight 3-circle lines: left slant, central vertical, right slant, middle horizontal, and bottom horizontal. Label the top circle T and the other six circles arbitrarily. From the text, the numbers 1 through 7 are used once, and each of the five lines has the same sum S. Add the five line sums. In the image, every non-top circle lies on exactly two of the five lines, while the top circle lies on three lines. Therefore the total of the five line sums is 2(1+2+3+4+5+6+7)+T = 56+T. Since this is also 5S, 56+T must be divisible by 5. Testing T among 1 to 7 gives only T=4.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram and label the circles: top T; middle-left A, center B, middle-right C; bottom-left D, bottom-middle E, bottom-right F. The five equal-sum lines visible are T-A-D, T-B-E, T-C-F, A-B-C, and D-E-F. Let their common sum be S. Add the two horizontal line equations: (A+B+C)+(D+E+F)=2S. These are exactly all numbers except T, so 2S=28-T. Next add the two sloping side equations: (T+A+D)+(T+C+F)=2S. Compare this with the two horizontal equations; the shared terms A,C,D,F cancel, giving 2T=B+E. The vertical line is T+B+E=S, so S=3T. Substitute into 2S=28-T to get 6T=28-T, hence 7T=28 and T=4.
